name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a D+13 partisan lean
Incumbent Ed Case is running and holds a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Adriel Lam has no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%
model.rationale: Hawaii's 1st District leans heavily Democratic, Ed Case is a well-funded incumbent seeking reelection, and his Republican opponent shows no measurable financial backing. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Democratic win, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending or an unexpected polling miss in a low-turnout Honolulu electorate could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ed Case, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in Hawaii's 1st District, a Honolulu-based seat that leans about thirteen points Democratic. He has raised roughly $1.1 million and holds about $600,000 on hand, while Republican Adriel Lam reports no fundraising and no outside spending on either side. A Green and an independent candidate are also on the ballot but lack visible resources.

No public general-election polls cover the race, and no expert raters have issued grades, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap. Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 96 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with Case expected to win by roughly twenty points.
